chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and another, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from Mansur ibn Hazim or someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (blessings of God upon him) said: 'The one who is attentive to the timings of salat will never fully indulge in the pleasures of the world.'

key_terms.اهْتَمَّ: To be attentive, concerned, to give importance to; implies active mindfulness, not mere performance
key_terms.لَذَّةُ الدُّنْيَا: The pleasures/delights of the temporal world (dunya); worldly enjoyments that distract from the hereafter
key_terms.مَوَاقِيتُ الصَّلَاةِ: The designated/prescribed times of salat (prayer); observing them is a jurisprudential obligation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn say about observing the prayer times and worldly pleasures?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) quotes Imam Zayn al-Abidin Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS), the fourth Imam, who teaches that true devotion to the prescribed times of prayer is incompatible with complete absorption in worldly pleasures. This saying reflects the Shia emphasis on salat not merely as ritual but as a constant re-orientation of one's consciousness away from the transient world toward the divine. The statement was addressed to the early Muslim community during a period when preoccupation with the material world was seen as a spiritual danger, and observing the prayer times served as a recurring corrective.
